<p><img src="/media/?type=post&id=102597&key=user_uploads%2F1373%2F31af3058-9bd9-48b5-8b9a-4840055d12f9&variant=large" alt="uploaded image" /></p>
<p>Our first product - EDDA - is a tiny robot that protects soldiers and critical assets from Group 1 suicide drones. We are building it small enough and cheap enough to put that protection on everything: every vehicle, every position, every asset. EDDA defeats fast group 1 threats that fielded systems consistently miss. Operators evaluating it have told us it's the only system that's stopped fast Group 1 - we'll let them speak for themselves when they can.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KBGBUmwgpL0">https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KBGBUmwgpL0</a></p>
<div class="embed-container youtube relative pb-[56.25%] h-0">

    </div>
<p>Why this? We were watching people die in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and ended up researching the state of the union on defeating suicide drones. It was insanely bad - over-focus on RF, EW, and larger systems - all with obvious flaws. Nothing was working, all demos were of slow speed or static drones. RF & EW are somewhere between dead-ends and table-stakes, and the larger systems had many flaws. So, we felt compelled to fix it.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PEgJkZTNcks">https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PEgJkZTNcks</a></p>
<div class="embed-container youtube relative pb-[56.25%] h-0">

    </div>
<p>The U.S. and allies are up-against this threat with no viable solution, until now. We have multiple contracts, and have sold and delivered multiple systems.</p>
<p>Our next 3 products follow the same vein - delivering working systems at low SWaPc.</p>
